ouder.specimen: LATEST REPORT WHERE THE CREW HAD TO ACT · FILED 26 AUGUST 2026 BOLKMS BK117C2, unscheduled landing · flight controls affected · hovering IN PLAIN ENGLISH, READ BY GLM-5.3-FLASH This was a police-type helicopter, a Bolkms BK117 C2, belonging to an operator using the code QR9R, and it had flown 5,866 hours. On 26 August 2026, during a short hover flight lasting about a tenth of an hour, the attitude and heading reference system failed. This unit tells the crew which way the helicopter is pointing, whether the nose is up or down, and whether it is rolled left or right. The failure affected the flight controls, so the crew made an unscheduled landing. A test flight afterwards found the system cutting out repeatedly while hovering, with warning flags on both primary flight displays. The mechanic removed and replaced the number one unit and ran a successful functional test. The report does not say who owns or operates the helicopter. Read when this report arrived, 14:55 · 9.6 s · its words, not the FAA’s. Linked terms open a Perplexity search in a new tab. Underlined words below open the trade’s own meaning. THE MECHANIC’S WORDS, AS FILED AHRS FAIL FLT 1. TEST FLIGHT EVAL FOUND AHRS DISC APPEARED MULTIPLE TIMES DURING A 0.2 HOVER FLIGHT. OTHER INDICATIONS WERE AS FOLLOWS: "Y","R", AND "P" IN AMBER ON BOTH PFDS, AND "ROLRAT DIS" ON LANE 2 SCROLL PAGE. ALL OTHER INDICATIONS APPEARED NORMAL WITH THE FLIGHT INSTRUMENTS DISPLAY OF INFORMATION. REMOVED AND REPLACED #1 AHRS IAW 34-22-00, 4-1. FUNCTIONAL TEST SUCCESSFULLY COMPLETED.
